title: Absolute vs Relative URLs 📍
description: Understand paths and how to link to pages within your site or across the web.

slides.title: What's a URL? 🤔
slides.content:
# Uniform Resource Locator

A URL is an address on the web. It can be:
- **Absolute:** The full path including protocol (`https://`), domain, and path.
- **Relative:** A path relative to the current page's location.

Choosing the right type affects portability and maintenance.

slides.title: Absolute URLs 🌍
slides.content: # The Full Address ```html Our Team ``` Includes: - Protocol (`https://`) - Domain (`www.example.com`) - Path (`/about/team.html`) Use absolute URLs when linking to a different website. They work from any location.

quizData.question: Which of the following is an absolute URL?
quizData.explanation: An absolute URL includes the protocol and domain name.

slides.title: Relative URLs 🏠
slides.content:
# Navigate Within Your Own Site

Relative URLs are shorter and refer to files in relation to the current page.

- **Same folder:** `href="about.html"`
- **Child folder:** `href="blog/post1.html"`
- **Parent folder:** `href="../index.html"`
- **Root‑relative:** `href="/images/logo.png"` (starts from the domain root)

Relative links make your site portable – if you change your domain name, internal links still work.

slides.title: Relative Paths in Action
slides.content: Given this folder structure: ``` / ├── index.html ├── about/ │ └── team.html └── images/ └── logo.png ``` From `index.html` to link to `team.html`: `Team` From `team.html` back to `index.html`: `Home`

slides.title: Root‑Relative vs Document‑Relative 🧭
slides.content:
# Two Flavours of Relative

- **Document‑relative:** `../images/pic.jpg` – navigates from the current file's directory.
- **Root‑relative:** `/images/pic.jpg` – navigates from the website's root folder.

Root‑relative is great for assets used across many pages (like logos or CSS files) because the path doesn't change regardless of the page's depth.

quizData.question: What does `../` mean in a relative URL?

options.text: Go to the root of the site

quizData.explanation: `../` moves to the parent directory. `../../` would go up two levels.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Root‑Relative for Global Assets

For your main stylesheet, use `<link href="/css/style.css">` instead of `../../css/style.css`. It's safer and easier to move pages around.
